scenario.fault_family: routing daemon down (redundancy loss, no user outage)
scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring raised a fabric alarm: super_spine_router_0 and BOTH leaf
routers each report their BGP session toward spine_router_0_0 going
down within seconds of each other. No user has complained -- pc_0_0
(10.0.0.2) and pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) still reach each other -- but the
fabric is now running without its usual redundancy. All of
spine_router_0_0's interfaces still show UP. Find what broke.

injection.action: kill the BGP routing daemon (and watchfrr) on spine_router_0_0

post_inject_check.expect: 0% loss   (still OK -- redundant fabric via spine_router_0_1)

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: spine_router_0_0 bgpd
Mechanism: spine_router_0_0 (AS 65100) peers with super_spine_router_0
  (172.16.0.0, AS 65000), leaf_router_0_0 (172.16.0.5, AS 65200) and
  leaf_router_0_1 (172.16.0.7, AS 65201). Killing bgpd tears down all
  three sessions at once (the peers see the TCP session close and fall
  to Idle/Active). The CLOS fabric is redundant: both leaves still peer
  with spine_router_0_1, so 10.0.0.0/24 and 10.0.1.0/24 stay reachable
  via the other spine and users see at most a brief blip. The impact is
  loss of path redundancy, not an outage.
Localization: spine_router_0_0
Root cause: bgpd not running on spine_router_0_0
Fix: restart FRR on spine_router_0_0 (`service frr restart`) -- the
  config persists in /etc/frr/frr.conf, so the restart restores all
  three sessions.

Observable note: bgpd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog),
so nothing respawns it (this kill pattern is lab-verified on this
fabric's leaf routers, 2026-07-03; the spines run the same image and
FRR config layout). vtysh remains responsive via zebra,
`show running-config` on spine_router_0_0 simply contains NO
`router bgp` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists bgpd. An agent
may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the bgp configuration
is missing/empty on spine_router_0_0" -- that is the same fault observed
at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`service frr restart` on spine_router_0_0. The persistent
/etc/frr/frr.conf brings bgpd back with its full neighbor configuration;
the sessions to the super-spine and both leaves re-establish and the
fabric regains its second spine path.
scoring_axes: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: all three peers (super-spine + both leaves) lost their session to spine_router_0_0 at once while end-to-end traffic keeps flowing
bonus-notes-redundancy: explains that reachability survives because spine_router_0_1 still carries both host prefixes (loss of redundancy, not an outage)

line.expect: 0% loss   (still OK -- redundant fabric via spine_router_0_1)

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The FRR BGP daemon (`bgpd`) and its supervisor (`watchfrr`) on `spine_router_0_0`. The `frr.service` systemd unit is in state `inactive (dead)`.

**Mechanism:** BGP sessions are TCP connections initiated to port 179. When `bgpd` is not running, no process is listening on port 179 on `spine_router_0_0`. Its three configured peers — `leaf_router_0_0`, `leaf_router_0_1`, and `super_spine_router_0` — each attempt to open a TCP session but receive no SYN-ACK. They enter the BGP `Active` state (retry loop), which is exactly what the fabric alarm reported. Because `watchfrr` is also absent, there is no FRR watchdog to detect the crash and attempt a restart.

**Localization:** Solely `spine_router_0_0`. All other routers (`spine_router_0_1`, both leaf routers, `super_spine_router_0`) show FRR healthy with `bgpd` and `watchfrr` running. `spine_router_0_1` has all three of its BGP sessions `Established`, so the alternate spine path carries the data plane — explaining why `pc_0_0` and `pc_0_1` still reach each other with 0% loss.

**Root cause:** The FRR service (`frr.service`) is stopped/dead on `spine_router_0_0`, taking `bgpd` down with it and rendering the router BGP-deaf. No configuration was corrupted; the configuration stored on disk is intact.

**Fix:** Restart the FRR service on `spine_router_0_0` with `systemctl start frr`. This will bring up `watchfrr`, `zebra`, and `bgpd` in order, re-establish the three dormant BGP sessions, and restore full fabric redundancy.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly localizes the fault to spine_router_0_0, stating the FRR/bgpd/watchfrr are down only on that device.
The report explicitly states bgpd is not running on spine_router_0_0 (FRR service inactive), satisfying the requirement to identify the BGP daemon as down.

per_axis.axis: must-distinguish-symptom-pattern: all three peers (super-spine + both leaves) lost their session to spine_router_0_0 at once while end-to-end traffic keeps flowing
per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly notes bgpd/watchfrr are down on spine_router_0_0 causing all three peers to lose sessions simultaneously and explains that spine_router_0_1 keeps data-plane traffic flowing, matching the symptom pattern.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-redundancy: explains that reachability survives because spine_router_0_1 still carries both host prefixes (loss of redundancy, not an outage)
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly notes spine_router_0_1 has all BGP sessions Established and carries the data plane, explaining reachability is preserved and this is a loss of redundancy rather than an outage.
Starting the frr service (systemctl start frr) will bring back watchfrr/bgpd and re-establish the BGP sessions, which matches the expected remediation.

The investigation log clearly shows bgpd/watchfrr absent, frr.service inactive, and no listener on port 179 while data-plane reachability is ok — supporting the daemon-down root cause. One minor ungrounded claim (asserting on-disk config intact / zebra alive) is not shown in the log but does not invalidate the main diagnosis.
